description: 🚀 ECHO NOVA is a beginner-friendly team for NASA Space Apps 2026. We love space, creativity, and storytelling. Our project, THE LAST SIGNAL, explores NASA’s Opportunity rover through an interactive story. We welcome beginners interested in web development, design, NASA research, and writing. No experience needed—just curiosity and teamwork!
summary:
Project Afterlight is an interactive educational website developed by Team EchoNova for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Inspired by the theme “Abandoned, But Not Forgotten,” the project focuses on spacecraft and missions that have been left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Many of these missions played an important role in space exploration, but their stories are often overlooked once their missions come to an end. We wanted to bring those stories back into focus.

Using real NASA mission information, we created an interactive platform where visitors can explore mission histories, discover where spacecraft were left behind, learn about their achievements, and take part in interactive activities.

Our aim is to make space exploration more engaging and accessible while helping people understand that even missions that have ended continue to contribute to scientific history.
details: What It Does Project Afterlight is an educational website that explores the stories of spacecraft and scientific equipment left behind during space exploration. It presents historical information through storytelling, visual elements, and interactive activities. The website includes the following features: 1. Mission Exploration Visitors can explore different space missions and learn about their objectives, achievements, challenges, and final stages. 2. Interactive Planetary Exploration The website provides a visual way to explore mission locations and discover where different spacecraft and equipment were left behind. 3. Mission Storytelling Each mission is presented through a structured story, covering its arrival, objectives, discoveries, final communication, and what remains today. 4. Interactive Activities The website includes a signal-reconnection puzzle and knowledge quizzes. These activities help visitors engage with the subject rather than simply reading information. Why We Created This Project Space exploration is often remembered through successful launches, major discoveries, and active missions. However, the spacecraft that completed their journeys are rarely discussed. We wanted to highlight these overlooked missions and show why they still matter. Every spacecraft has a story, and even after its mission ends, its contribution to science and exploration remains. Through Project Afterlight, we hope to make space history interesting and accessible, especially for students and people who are curious about science and technology. Technologies and Resources Used - HTML: To structure the website and its content. - CSS: To create the visual design, animations, and responsive layout. - JavaScript: To develop interactive features, puzzles, and quizzes. - GitHub: For project code management. - GitHub Pages: To host and publish the website. - NASA Resources: Official NASA mission archives, images, and scientific information for research and reference. Our Approach From the beginning, we wanted Project Afterlight to be more than a collection of mission facts. We wanted visitors to feel like they were exploring an archive of forgotten space missions. We focused on combining research, storytelling, and interactive web design to create an experience that is both informative and engaging. The visual design and atmosphere were developed around the central idea of the project: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten. Project Afterlight is our attempt to bring attention to the machines that once explored other worlds and remind people that their stories deserve to be remembered.
